reden: Not detected. The described issue concerns LibProving/LibVerifying slashing/refund logic: when a higher-tier/guardian proof overrides earlier proofs, ts.prover and bonds are overwritten so earlier correct provers/contesters lose validity/contest bonds, and guardians can only trigger liveness-bond refunds (RETURN_LIVENESS_BOND). The final refund in LibVerifying goes to ts.prover (often the guardian), leaving earlier bonds unrecoverable. None of the audit findings matches this mechanism. The closest items are (1) “Guardian re-prove branch always panics” (an assert logic bug preventing re-prove) and (2) “GuardianProver approval hash omits proof data” (allows a single guardian to decide liveness bond refund). Both are different root causes and fixes; they do not address wrongful slashing/refunding of validity/contest bonds or history-insensitive refunding. Therefore the specific vulnerability was not reported.
